requirement:
`habeas mdbook` MUST automatically generate exactly one execution-coverage
subchapter under the requirements index of
{cite}`requirements.index.chapter`, whether that requirements index is
explicitly placed or automatically generated.
rationale:
I judged this from the supplied test sources only. I did not request implementation source.

**Obligation.** `habeas mdbook` MUST generate exactly one execution-coverage subchapter under the requirements index. This must hold when the index is explicitly placed and when it is automatically generated.

**Explicit index.** `src/index.rs#mod[tests]/fn[index_shows_evidence_states_and_links_generated_chapters]` builds a book with a chapter containing `:::{requirements-index}`. After `preprocess_book`, it does the following:
- It filters the index's `sub_items` for chapters named "Coverage gaps" and asserts the count is exactly 1.
- It asserts that chapter's path is `appendix/requirements-index/coverage.md` and its `parent_names` is `["Requirements index"]`.
- It asserts the index content links to `requirements-index/coverage.html`.
- It asserts `index.sub_items.len() == 6`: five requirement detail pages plus the single coverage chapter.

**Automatic index.** `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[definitions_without_a_marker_get_a_default_index_and_detail_pages]` has no marker, so the index is generated. It asserts the following:
- The generated top-level "Requirements index" holds exactly one "Coverage gaps" subchapter. That chapter has path `requirements-index/coverage.md` and `parent_names` `["Requirements index"]`.
- The index links to it.
- All the other children are detail pages, matched by an exact name list. The list has no duplicate coverage chapter.

**Hierarchy of the generated reports.** `src/execution_coverage/book.rs#mod[tests]/fn[generated_reports_inherit_the_requirements_index_hierarchy]` runs the production `populate_in` with the index both numbered and unnumbered. It checks the following:
- The coverage chapter sits under the index.
- Its path, `parent_names` and section number are correct.
- The parent has exactly 2 sub-items: the pre-existing Guide chapter and the one coverage chapter.
- The coverage chapter's own generated pages inherit that hierarchy.
- The generated guidance text is present.

**Supporting test.** `src/execution_coverage/book.rs#mod[tests]/fn[filtered_runs_union_latest_attempts_and_invalidate_with_saved_source]` exercises the content of the coverage chapter. It also asserts that the `{coverage-index}` directive is replaced.

**Conclusion.** Both required cases, explicit and automatic, are covered. The "exactly one" cardinality is asserted in each, and so are placement under the index and the index's link to the chapter. I found no plausible violation, such as zero or duplicate chapters or the wrong parent, that these tests would accept. The cited `requirements.index.chapter` behaviour, directive replacement and default generation, is exercised in the same tests, so applying it in this case is covered.

text: `habeas mdbook` MUST automatically generate exactly one execution-coverage
subchapter under the requirements index of

An mdBook chapter MAY contain one standalone `{requirements-index}` directive with an empty body, opened by at least three colons and closed by at least as many. A book MUST contain no more than one such directive. `habeas mdbook` MUST render a requirements index listing all requirements defined in rendered chapters, each linking to its evidence detail page under {cite}`requirements.index.detail_pages`. When a directive is present, it MUST replace the directive with the index table; otherwise, it MUST generate the chapter specified by {cite}`requirements.index.chapter.default`.
